description: verification-architecture.md's R6 proof-table row (line 37), even after the iteration-3 fix for FIND-007, contains no fixture or assertion anywhere that proves the 4000-character UPPER cap on `detail` (mandated by behavioral-spec.md R6 line 143: 'capped at 4000 characters') actually engages. FIND-007's fix corrected the LOWER-boundary problem (a fixture in the 181-900 range could not distinguish a correct 4000-cap impl from a wrongly-900-capped impl) by widening the skill_error fixture to '>2000-char stdout' and asserting `detail` is 'LONGER than 900 chars' while `ledger.jsonl`'s `result` for the same wake stays capped at 900. That new assertion correctly rules out an implementation that (bug) reuses the existing 900-char cap for `detail`. But it does NOT rule out the opposite-direction bug: an implementation that forgets to cap `detail` at 4000 at all (unbounded pass-through), or that caps it at some other wrong ceiling (e.g. 10000). Every fixture actually specified in the R6 row -- the skill_error case ('>2000-char stdout' -> 'LONGER than 900 chars') and the wake_error case ('detail up to 4000 chars', described only as a shape, never as a boundary assertion with an oversized fixture) -- uses an input strictly under 4000 characters (post-redaction/whitespace-collapse). Because no fixture anywhere in R1-R10 supplies raw content that EXCEEDS 4000 characters and then asserts `detail.length === 4000` (or `<= 4000` with content demonstrably truncated relative to the raw input), a Phase 2b implementation that stores `detail` uncapped, or caps it at any value >= ~2001 chars, would pass every assertion currently specified for R6 while silently violating the requirement text's own '4000 characters' hard cap and by extension the unstated-but-implied 'do not let one giant stdout blow out harness-failures.jsonl file size unbounded' rationale that is the entire reason a cap exists in the first place (mirrors the Problem section's own concern about `result`'s cap. i.e. the same class of concern R6 exists to guard against, just at the opposite boundary from FIND-007). This is the same failure mode class as FIND-007 (a proof-table cell whose literal fixture range cannot distinguish correct-vs-incorrect implementations at a specific numeric boundary the requirement itself asserts), just at the boundary FIND-007's fix did not touch. Note by contrast: R5's proof-table row explicitly tests 'one below threshold -> false; exactly at threshold -> true; one above threshold -> true' -- the project's own established rigor pattern for numeric-boundary requirements -- which R6's 4000-char ceiling does not receive anywhere in the table. Fix: add an explicit fixture to the R6 row, e.g. 'simulate one skill_error wake whose (pre-cap, post-redaction) output exceeds 4000 characters (e.g. 6000 chars) -> `detail.length === 4000` exactly, and the retained content is the first/expected 4000 chars of the source string (not silently unbounded, not silently truncated to some other length)'.

evidence.snippet: detail up to 4000 chars; ... simulate one skill_error wake (mock skill exits 1 with a >2000-char stdout ...)->one line with slot,layer:'tool_logic',exit_code,detail LONGER than 900 chars ... assert ledger.jsonl's own result field ... is capped at 900 chars while harness-failures.jsonl's detail field ... is NOT truncated at 900 -- no fixture or assertion in this row ever exceeds 4000 raw chars or asserts detail.length===4000
